explanations.explanation: That's exactly how the LORD opens: “I have loved you,” says the LORD. (Malachi 1:2) Before any burden gets unpacked, before any question gets asked, He says that first. Friend, if somebody opens with those words, you lean in and listen.
Not quite, baker. The LORD never says He has left them in these verses. His first words are “I have loved you,” says the LORD. (Malachi 1:2) That's the starting point for everything else He says.

I get why you'd guess that, since a burden sounds heavy. But the LORD doesn't open with judging Israel. He opens with “I have loved you,” says the LORD. (Malachi 1:2) Everything else in the passage comes after those words.

Yes, and Israel doesn't waste a second. The LORD says He has loved them, and they ask, “How have You loved us?” (Malachi 1:2) That's a real question from the people, right in the middle of the LORD's words. I think they wanted Him to show them.
This one is true, baker. Israel does answer, and they answer with a question: “How have You loved us?” (Malachi 1:2) They don't just nod along. The LORD hears the question and gives them an answer.

Jacob it is. The LORD says, “Yet Jacob I have loved…” (Malachi 1:2) Jacob is the one God later renamed Israel (Genesis 35:10), so the LORD is talking to Jacob's own family line. That's the whole point of the question He asks.

That's the other brother, friend. Esau is the one the LORD mentions when He says, “…but Esau I have hated…” (Malachi 1:3) The love He names in Malachi 1:2 goes to Jacob: “Yet Jacob I have loved.” Two brothers can get mixed up fast, so no shame in it.

Close family, but not the one. Isaac was Jacob and Esau's father (Genesis 25:24-26), and he isn't named in these verses. The LORD points to the two brothers and says, “Yet Jacob I have loved.” (Malachi 1:2)

Wasteland is the word. The LORD says, “…I have made his mountains a wasteland and left his inheritance to the desert jackals.” (Malachi 1:3) Mountains that should be solid and lasting, and the jackals get the inheritance. That's a picture with nothing left in it.

A garden would be a nice change, baker, but that's not what the LORD says. He says He made Esau's mountains “a wasteland,” and the inheritance went to the desert jackals. (Malachi 1:3) Jackals don't hang around gardens looking for a place to settle.

A fortress sounds strong, but that's the opposite of this verse. The LORD says He made Esau's mountains “a wasteland” and left his inheritance to the desert jackals. (Malachi 1:3) Nobody is holding anything down up there.

explanations.answer: He will tear down what they build
explanations.explanation: That's it. The LORD of Hosts says, “They may build, but I will demolish.” (Malachi 1:4) Edom, Esau's people, has plans to rebuild, but the LORD says what He will do about them. Rebuilding is a lot of work, and I wouldn't want to hear that part.

explanations.answer: He will help them build it back
explanations.explanation: I love the hopeful thinking, friend, but the LORD says the opposite. His words are, “They may build, but I will demolish.” (Malachi 1:4) Edom, Esau's people, gets no building help here.

explanations.answer: He will let them build in peace
explanations.explanation: Peaceful building would be nice, baker, but that's not what He says. The LORD of Hosts says, “They may build, but I will demolish.” (Malachi 1:4) Edom can pick up the hammers, and the LORD still says what comes next.

Not this time, baker. The LORD doesn't say a little while. He says Edom will be “a people with whom the LORD is indignant forever.” (Malachi 1:4) That word forever is right there in the verse, so it's easy to skate past.

Right, it's false. The LORD says Edom will be called the Land of Wickedness and “a people with whom the LORD is indignant forever.” (Malachi 1:4) Forever is a long way from a little while. That's what the text says, and I'll leave it right there.

explanations.answer: He is great even beyond Israel
explanations.explanation: Yes, and what a line. The LORD says Israel will see this with their own eyes and say, “The LORD is great—even beyond the borders of Israel.” (Malachi 1:5) They won't just hear about it, they'll watch it happen. Friend, that's a big sentence about a big God.

explanations.answer: He is great only inside Israel
explanations.explanation: That's backwards, baker. The LORD says they will say, “The LORD is great—even beyond the borders of Israel.” (Malachi 1:5) Beyond is the key word. The borders don't box Him in.

explanations.answer: He has stepped away from Israel
explanations.explanation: Nope, nothing like that in these verses. The LORD says Israel will see it for themselves and say, “The LORD is great—even beyond the borders of Israel.” (Malachi 1:5) He opened this whole passage with “I have loved you,” so stepping away isn't where it ends. (Malachi 1:2)
